It depends on the project. The ones I have already shipped are listed under Tools.
Tell me what you need, who it is for and by when. I reply with the questions still open and a proposal.

method.label: Method
method.title: How I work
method.lead: Five stages, from idea to working software.

phases.name: Understand
phases.title: Before writing code, I listen.
phases.body: I start from the people who will use the software and what has to change in their day. Together we sort out what is really needed, what can wait and what stays out.
practices: Time and cost with honest margins

phases.name: Design
phases.title: Simple choices, explained in writing.
phases.body: I pick the simplest solution that does the job, not the fashionable one. Important decisions are written down, so whoever comes next knows why things are the way they are.
practices: Security and data planned from day one

phases.name: Build
phases.title: One piece at a time, always checked.
phases.body: I work in small steps, and every step can be seen and tried. Each change is reviewed before it reaches the real version, and nothing gets lost.
practices: A full history of every change

phases.name: Release
phases.title: Going live without surprises.
phases.body: Before reaching users, the software goes through a series of automatic checks. New features reach a few people at a time: if something is wrong, it rolls back on its own.
practices: New features to a few users at a time

phases.name: Maintain
phases.title: The work goes on after launch.
phases.body: I keep an eye on speed and errors and get an alert before a problem reaches you or your customers. Everything is documented for you: the software stays yours.
practices: Alerts before it becomes a problem

principles.title: Secure from the start
principles.body: Passwords and sensitive data protected, access only for those who need it, everything kept up to date.

principles.title: Simple first
principles.body: No needless complexity: the simpler the software, the less it breaks and the less it costs to maintain.

principles.title: Fast, and measured
principles.body: Pages and apps that open straight away. Checked with real numbers, not by feel.

principles.title: Usable by everyone
principles.body: Readable text, keyboard controls, works with the tools people with low vision rely on.

principles.title: Always in the loop
principles.body: Updates on a fixed schedule, and a heads-up as soon as something changes.

principles.title: Built to last
principles.body: Tidy, documented code: another developer can pick it up without starting over.

process.title: How I work
process.lead: Four steps, from the first message to software you use every day.

steps.name: Listen
steps.title: First of all, I listen.
steps.body: A call to understand who will use the software, what it must solve and what can wait. No jargon.
steps.get: a clear quote, with time and cost.

steps.name: Prototype
steps.title: Then I show you what it will be.
steps.body: Before writing code I prepare a prototype you can click, on computer and phone. Changes happen now, while they are cheap.
steps.get: a prototype to try and comment on.

steps.name: Build
steps.title: I build, and you watch it grow.
steps.body: I work in short stages. At each one you get a new version to try, and we decide the next step together.
steps.get: regular updates and an always-on preview link.

steps.name: Live
steps.title: It goes live, and I stay.
steps.body: I publish the software, keep an eye on it and update it when needed. Documentation and code stay with you.
